newsitem.title: USA: Bulgaria debt sinks on possible future default.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria debt sinks on possible future default.

text.p: Bulgarian debt prices tumbled following comments by Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov that the country may have to default on future debt payments unless it receives help to pull the country out of economic crisis.

"The situation in Bulgaria continues to deteriorate. The news has added further fuel to what people already believed," said one emerging market debt trader at a U.S. investment firm who attributed the losses to news of a possible default.
Bulgarian IABs sank 1-3/4 to 46-3/4, its FLRBs tumbled two percentage points to 33-1/2 bid and discount bonds fell 1-1/4 to 52-1/4 bid.

Stoyanov told NATO Ambassadors in Brussels Wednesday that a default and a moratorium on the country's payments was not out of the question since payments on its extrenal debt due later this year could trigger a final collapse in the country's financial system.
In addition, Stoyanov said "unpredictable social consequences" would follow if the economic crisis was worsened by meeting its international debt obligations.
Although Bulgaria made a $135 million payment on its Brady debt Tuesday, sources said it does not ensure future payments given the country's current economic and potitical crisis.

"I continue to believe that the country is in a difficult situation and even the payment now at the end of January is not proof that they are capable of paying in the future," said Kurt Schmid, executive vice president and head of proprietary trading at SBC Warburg in New York.
Bulgaria -- with hyperinflation, rapid depreciation of its currency, a very weak banking sector and extremely high interest rates -- is facing an economic meltdown, sources said
At the same time, they said the government is not in a position to take the measures recommended by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) given the current political problems.

"The delay in taking forceful and cohesive actions as recommended by the IMF has resulted in a significant deterioration and as we all know that can get really out of control, so even if they do take the necessary action it might be too late," Schmid said.
Bulgaria was hit with anti-government strikes for the 24th day Wednesday as workers joined students and opposition parties demanding elections to pull the country out of crisis.
"It is a serious risk and it has been a risk for quite awhile so I was surpised to see relatively high prices in the Brady market in spite of the risks," Schmid said.
"It is a very difficult situation and it doesn't seem like there is going to be a solution any time soon," another emerging market debt source added.
